items.text: President Trump's Executive Order to freeze federal funding is another example of a self-inflicted disaster. Issuing vague guidance leaves the impact and implementation open for interpretation. The WH is "unsure" if this EO will shut down access to Medicaid, which affects tens of millions of Americans. I urge President Trump to reverse course so that the American people are not negatively impacted by this decision.

Today, I announced a bill to broaden health care coverage due to Alabama's refusal to expand Medicaid. This issue is one of my top priorities, and this bill is a step in the right direction. Find out more about the bill here: https://t.co/nlrmtlHnLX https://t.co/LZGf0ZpQLb

This week, I spoke with @ALDailyNews to discuss the COVER Now Act, which would broaden healthcare coverage for over 300,000 Alabamians due to the state’s refusal to expand Medicaid. Click the link to read the full article. 
https://t.co/sHsfeOj1c2

I ended last week in the district with community leaders from Washington and Clarke Counties. I'm thankful for these important conversations to discuss how we can work together to improve rural infrastructure, health care, and the workforce. https://t.co/jz0k2OZYmy

The House Republicans’ budget bill is bad for Alabama’s Second Congressional District. 

This budget cuts vital programs like Medicaid and SNAP while adding at least $2 trillion to our national debt and giving tax breaks to the ultra-wealthy. 

If you show me where you spend your time and your money, I will show you your priorities. It is clear from this budget that the everyday Americans in Alabama are not a priority. I’m voting against it.

The President’s speech last night was just more rambling lies with no care or concern for everyday people. Touting policies like retaliatory tariffs that do nothing but drive up costs for consumers and businesses. Putting critical programs like Medicaid and SNAP on the chopping block while making the ultra wealthy even richer. It’s clear this Administration will continue to ignore the needs of the everyday Americans.

I voted no on the Republicans’ continuing resolution because it: 

❌ Cuts $23B in medical care for veterans 
❌ Cuts food assistance for hundreds of thousands of seniors
❌ Cuts funding for disaster relief months before hurricane season, which directly impacts cities like Mobile that are frequently hit with natural disasters.
Read my full statement: https://t.co/g8iPqgPGhG

Thank you, to all the community leaders in Pike County, for meeting with me today. Our discussions focused on improving rural infrastructure, education, and keeping our rural hospitals open. https://t.co/4XgLgmDU8j

I met with the Rural Division of the Alabama Hospital Association to discuss how we can improve rural healthcare across the district. Too many communities have lost/are at risk of losing their hospital. This is unacceptable, and we are committed to saving our hospitals. https://t.co/d5swfV8T12
The stupidity continues, Trump just cut almost $200 MILLION from Alabama healthcare. Reminder: Alabama has basically the worst health outcomes in the country and this will make it worse.

Thank you to the DaVita Majestic Dialysis Center for giving me a tour of their facility this week. Without Medicaid, some patients could not afford weekly treatments. This is why I will keep fighting to protect and expand Medicaid in Alabama. https://t.co/GqfF4lqF2l

Rural communities are facing dire circumstances—especially in my district. Hospitals continue to close, effectively cutting off healthcare access and eliminating jobs for people across the country. This cannot continue. 
 
That is why I am introducing the bipartisan Rural Hospital Stabilization Act of 2025 with @RepBrianJack. This bill will provide critical funding to help rural hospitals remain open and serve the people who need it the most.

Taking away access to Medicaid and SNAP for those who need it most just to benefit the very rich is not worth it, and it never will be. That’s why I voted no on the Republicans’ budget bill. https://t.co/OQNDSmJhmo

Protecting SNAP and Medicaid is not about politics. We are not in a position where we can’t afford it. We are spending almost $4 million on every trip that Donald Trump takes to Mar-a-Lago.
 
It’s not a question of resources. It’s a question of priorities. https://t.co/hBbFgN9lKp

I’m on the floor this morning supporting Leader @RepJeffries, who is speaking the truth about this trash bill. Republicans have the opportunity to do the right thing. But know that if they don’t, Dems will keep fighting for you because taking away health care from 17 million people ain’t right.

For 60 years, Medicare and Medicaid have been lifelines for millions of Americans, created out of necessity to ensure access to healthcare for seniors, families, and our most vulnerable. I'm committed to the fight to protect and expand these programs, especially for those in District 2 and across Alabama.  #Medicare60

I led a virtual meeting with 2nd District mayors and county officials last night to brief them on the Shutdown as it approaches the 30 day mark and discuss the path forward. The consequences are real for our community: federal workers are not being paid; healthcare costs are set to at least double for approximately 50,000 people in the District, and nearly 1 in 4 residents risk losing the ability to put food on the table just before Thanksgiving because the Trump Administration refuses to use available funds. We deserve better than this. And I will keep fighting for what's right for our District and for Alabama.

House Democrats just spent the better part of the last 40-plus days trying to keep healthcare affordable for millions of Americans while our House Republican colleagues were on a taxpayer funded vacation. 

During this shutdown, realities hit home for a lot of people. And for what, in the end? What were Republicans able to give in the end? Nothing but a handshake deal to take a future vote on extending the healthcare subsidies when we all know that future vote is the equivalent of asking two wolves and a chicken to vote on what’s for dinner.

It is dead on arrival. It is dead on arrival.

I have about 50,000 people in my district who are slated to see their healthcare premiums on average nearly double. And this is in a district where the individual median income is just north of $32,000. I have 13 counties in my district, 10 of them either do not have a hospital because it has recently closed, or their hospital is on literal life support, and they have to go to a county commission or a city council every single month to make payroll. And the largest hospital in Montgomery, Alabama – the state’s capital – is in the midst of a bankruptcy and also risks of closure. 

And this is all in a state that has the third lowest life expectancy in the country. So, healthcare for us is not a talking point. Protecting healthcare for us is a requisite. It’s a requirement. It’s something we have to do.

I’m proud to share that I helped secure $1 MILLION for Jackson Medical Center in Clarke County! It will be used to purchase advanced diagnostic imaging equipment, repair and renovate infrastructure, and improve security for patients and staff. This is a big win for rural healthcare in Jackson and the entire region! 

Rural hospitals across AL-2 face serious challenges daily, with many at risk of closing due to financial pressures. This funding for Jackson is a step in the right direction, and I will continue fighting to protect our hospitals so every family has access to quality healthcare.
